object_description: large compact block with three patios and an outer layer of external escape routes
design_condition: the complex is concentrated on the western edge of the site, with the courts stepped into the sloping terrain and a park-like strip mediating towards the neighbourhood

positive: Park-like space with play and recreation facilities mediates between the neighbourhood and the school complex
Open space concept carefully worked out, showing a good understanding of the needs of the pupils
The gradation of levels allows ideal connections and accessibility from all sides
External escape routes form a light and playful outer layer mediating between inside and outside
Three spacious patios bring plenty of daylight to the classroom level
Patios together with the outdoor workspaces form an exciting learning landscape of heated and unheated rooms
Top-lit assembly hall and connecting staircase give the three floors a versatile centre function
Visual relation between gymnasium and auditorium recognised as an independent, pedagogically valuable idea
The bipolar centre gives the school a strong, unmistakable identity
Construction costs and climate-relevant envelope surfaces are in the middle range
negative: The striking jump in height and the monumental staircase are not convincing
Expansion of car and bicycle parking spaces is not shown
Third gymnasium under the all-weather pitch is unrealistically expensive and unsuitable in lighting terms
Ambivalence between the light escape layer and the heavy concrete hall structures irritated the jury
Classrooms and group rooms are furnished stereotypically; forward-looking forms of learning are not stimulated
The centre idea sacrifices natural lighting and ventilation of the gymnasium
Fully glazed exterior walls are disadvantageous for furnishing classrooms and special rooms
Very few toilet facilities, an outdoor equipment room and teacher teamwork rooms are missing
Access to the roofscape is not proposed
Escape routes in the eastern area of the ground floor remain unresolved
Some required rooms are missing or too small; access zones and technical rooms potentially too small
The building services would significantly change the architectural expression
The very large roof area would probably need greening in combination with photovoltaics
